question: Loperamide is contraindicated in bloody (dysenteric) diarrhoea because reducing gut motility may allow invasive pathogens to remain in contact with the mucosa longer, worsening the infection.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Loperamide slows gut transit by activating μ-opioid receptors in the enteric nervous system. While beneficial in non-inflammatory secretory diarrhoea, this property is dangerous when invasive bacteria are present — dysentery is an absolute contraindication.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. In bloody diarrhoea caused by invasive pathogens such as Shigella, EHEC, or Salmonella, loperamide's motility-reducing effect prolongs mucosal contact time, facilitating deeper tissue invasion and potentially precipitating toxic megacolon or systemic bacteraemia.
